# Rosalind Penrose

## Overview

- **Age:** Forty-five years old (at the time of volume 2)  <sub>[v2 c21 P34](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0034)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v2 c21 P34](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0034), [v2 c21 P44](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0044)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Miss Rosalind  <sub>[v2 c21 P34](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0034), [v2 c21 P40](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0040), [v2 c21 P43](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0043)</sub>

## Appearance

Rosalind is a tiny woman with thick, lovely, wavy snow-white hair styled in flattering puffs and coils. Below her hair is an almost youthful face featuring bright, wood-brown eyes with tiny gold flecks, rosy cheeks, and sweet lips. Her voice has been described as recalling white satin, splashing water, and fairy bells.

_Sources: [v2 c22 P2](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0002), [v2 c21 P45](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0045)_

## Personality

Rosalind possesses a distinct, somewhat unconventional charm and an imaginative nature that leads some local residents to consider her peculiar. Though she leads a secluded life, she is warm, hospitable, and friendly, delighting in welcoming visitors to her home for tea. She harbors a gentle sentimentality and deep devotion to those she loves, though she can show nervousness and emotional vulnerability when confronted with painful memories of her past.

_Sources: [v2 c22 P3](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0003), [v2 c22 P6](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0006), [v2 c22 P7](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0007), [v2 c21 P42](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0042), [v2 c21 P87](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0087), [v2 c28 P57](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0057)_

## Traits

- Imaginative and fond of creative play
- Hospitable and welcoming  <sub>[v2 c21 P42](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0042), [v2 c21 P78](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0078)</sub>
- Sensitive and emotional  <sub>[v2 c21 P87](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0087), [v2 c28 P57](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0057)</sub>

## History

Rosalind Penrose grew up in an isolated, ivy-draped sandstone house built by her father near the Welby River. In her youth, she was considered a beauty and became betrothed to Stephen Stanhope; however, after a severe disagreement broke their engagement twenty-five years prior, Stephen left for the United States, and Rosalind gradually withdrew from social life. Residing quietly at Echo Cottage with her young handmaiden, Belinda the Fourth, she remained largely forgotten by the broader community until Nell Harcourt and Isolde Pembroke paid her a visit. During their tea, Rosalind learned that her former fiancé's son, Cedric Stanhope, was being taught by Nell in Brierley. Nell later intercepted the mail to help facilitate a reunion between Stephen and Rosalind. Anticipating Stephen's evening visit, Rosalind dressed nervously in her forget-me-not organdy gown to meet him.

_Sources: [v2 c22 P3](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0003), [v2 c22 P7](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0007), [v2 c22 P9](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0009), [v2 c21 P31](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0031), [v2 c21 P36](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0036), [v2 c21 P81](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0081), [v2 c21 P83](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0083), [v2 c28 P45](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0045), [v2 c28 P54](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0054), [v2 c28 P57](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0057)_

## Background by volume

- Daughter of old Mr. Penrose who built the stone house eighty years ago after arriving from England  <sub>[v2 c22 P7](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0007)</sub>
- Named Rosalind by her father after lavender-scented sheets kept him awake thinking of her mother in East Welby  <sub>[v2 c21 P86](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0086)</sub>
- Was betrothed to Stephen Stanhope twenty-five years prior before their engagement abruptly ended  <sub>[v2 c22 P9](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0009), [v2 c21 P36](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0036)</sub>

## Quotes

> Will you not visit me once more?  <sub>[v2 c21 P78](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0078)</sub>
